title: A Daily Routine at the Family Business

context.topic: A typical workday at a small family business
context.purpose: Reinforce present forms of the main verb be, everyday uses of 'move on', and familiar family collocations such as 'family business' and 'family dinner' in a practical workplace context.

sentences.text: Every morning, Daniel arrives at the family business at nine o’clock.
He is usually the first person in the office, so the room is quiet.
notes: The present form 'is' describes Daniel's usual situation.

sentences.text: His sister is responsible for customer emails, and their father is in charge of the shop.
Before they start work, they are often busy planning the day.
At ten, Daniel checks the orders and answers questions from customers.
Sometimes a problem takes longer than expected, but he tries to stay calm.
When one task is finished, he moves on to the next one.
notes: 'Move on to' means to proceed to another task or stage.

sentences.text: His sister helps him when the office is especially busy.
At lunch, the family usually eats together in the small kitchen.
They talk about work, family life, and their plans for the weekend.
After lunch, Daniel returns to his desk and finishes the urgent orders.
If a customer is unhappy, he listens carefully and looks for a practical solution.
At five o’clock, the shop is quieter and most of the work is complete.
Daniel writes a short list for tomorrow before he leaves.
In the evening, he is happy to move on from work and enjoy time at home.
notes: Here, 'move on from work' means to stop focusing on work and turn to something else.

sentences.text: Sometimes the family has dinner together, and Daniel feels ready for another day.

notes: UK IPA fields are left empty rather than supplying unverified transcriptions.
